technical_and_design_decisions: The target repository is the Spring Cloud Stream apps repository (s-c-s); modules are implemented as standard Spring Cloud Stream binder-agnostic apps following the existing conventions of that repository.
Each ported module is implemented as a dedicated Maven module with its own POM, consistent with the multi-module structure of the s-c-s repo.

Modules U1, U2, U3, U4, U6 are implemented as sinks (consumer producers producing output to an external system), while U5 (rabbit) is implemented as a source (consuming from RabbitMQ and emitting to the stream).
All modules use Spring Cloud Stream's annotation-based programming model (e.g., @EnableBinding, @StreamListener, Supplier) and re-use the Spring Integration adapter layer where applicable.

The original Spring XD module classes (configurers, options metadata, plugin metadata) are not re-used verbatim; instead, the underlying Spring Integration / client-library logic is reproduced using Spring Cloud Stream constructs (e.g., @ServiceActivator, MessageHandler beans).

For U7, support is added by allowing the HDFS module to be configured with classpath coordinates compatible with the latest HDP/PHD versions, and by validating against those cluster versions in test pipelines.
For U8, the migration guide is authored in AsciiDoc (the standard for Spring reference documentation) and published in the project's reference docs section.
assumptions: The developer has prior familiarity with Spring XD, Spring Integration, Spring Cloud Stream, and the target external systems (RabbitMQ, Redis, GemFire, FTP, file, HDFS).

Reference implementations of the corresponding Spring XD modules already exist and are accessible as a starting point, but cannot be dropped in unchanged because of API differences between XD and Spring Cloud Stream.

The s-c-s repository's build, parent POM, and existing modules already provide a working template (Whitelabel, simple-messaging patterns) that the new modules can mirror, so no large infrastructure work is required.

No new external dependencies beyond those already used in the XD counterparts are needed; transport libraries (e.g., Spring AMQP, Spring Data Redis, Spring Data GemFire, Apache Commons Net for FTP) are reused.
Each module includes its own unit and integration tests, but no large new test infrastructure has to be built.
The HDP/PHD version matrix is limited to a small set (e.g., HDP 2.6.x and PHD 1.x) and validation is done against a representative HDFS endpoint rather than full cluster provisioning.

Effort figures represent hands-on development time (analysis, coding, testing, documentation, review) performed by a single experienced developer; they do not include requirements elicitation, stakeholder meetings, or release management.

activities.activity_description: Create new module directories under the s-c-s multi-module project, register them in the parent POM, define dependencies, and verify the modules build and package successfully as part of the reactor build.

Analyze the Spring XD router module behavior (expression-based routing to named channels), re-implement it as a Spring Cloud Stream sink that evaluates a SpEL/expression on incoming messages and routes them to a downstream binding, with corresponding unit tests.

Re-implement the XD file sink (writing message payload to a file, with options for directory, name, suffix, charset, binary mode, rolling strategy) as a Spring Cloud Stream sink backed by a Spring Integration @ServiceActivator, with unit and integration tests against a temporary directory.

Re-implement the XD FTP sink (uploading files to a remote FTP server using Apache Commons Net, supporting factory beans, remote directory, file name expression, and binary/ASCII modes) as a Spring Cloud Stream sink, with tests using an embedded FTP server.

Re-implement the XD Redis sink (publishing messages to a Redis channel or storing them in a list using Spring Data Redis, with options for key, queue, and serialization) as a Spring Cloud Stream sink, with unit tests using an embedded Redis or testcontainers.

Re-implement the XD Rabbit source (consuming from a queue or exchange, with reconnection, ack/nack, and option mapping) as a Spring Cloud Stream source using Spring AMQP, with unit and integration tests against a real or embedded broker.

Re-implement the XD GemFire sink (writing payloads to a region, with key expression, region name, and cache/peer/locator configuration) as a Spring Cloud Stream sink backed by Spring Data GemFire, with unit tests and a smoke test against an embedded GemFire instance.

activities.activity_name: HDP/PHD distribution support for HDFS pipelines (U7)
activities.activity_description: Update the HDFS module (and any related sink configuration metadata) so that it works against the latest HDP and PHD distributions: verify Hadoop client compatibility, adjust classpath dependencies, and run integration tests against representative HDFS endpoints for those distros.

Research and write a migration guide section for the reference documentation covering breaking changes between Spring XD-based 1.2 modules and the new 1.3 Spring Cloud Stream modules (configuration property renames, option mapping, deployment/registration changes, runtime considerations).

Build representative streaming pipelines that combine the new modules (e.g., rabbit source -> router -> file/redis/ftp sink) to validate that they work together as a coherent set, and capture test output in the module documentation.

activities.activity_name: Code review, bug fixing, and final polish
activities.activity_description: Self-review all new modules, address review comments, fix issues found by the integration tests, ensure consistent code style and logging, and finalize the migration documentation cross-references.
